newsitem.title: Philippines: Philippine peso ends up despite rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up despite rate cuts.

text.p: *More dollar inflows seen due to APEC
The Philippine peso closed higher
at 26.266 to the dollar on Tuesday from 26.278, as dollar
inflows
outweighed the impact of the Central Bank's interest rate cut,
traders said.
"It should have been a go for a stronger dollar. But this
did
not materialize," a dealer from a big bank said. The Central
Bank
early in the day lowered its overnight borrowing rate to 10.75
from 11 percent and its lending to 13.25 from 14 percent.
The day's average, however, showed a weaker peso at 26.266 from 26.254 because the previous session had more deals for the same-day delivery of dollars, traders said.
Volume thinned to $108.9 million from $220.5 million.
"They're (banks) liquid in dollars. They don't want to hold on to dollars," the traders said.
Banks are anticipating more dollar inflows following the success of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit meeting held in Manila, traders said.
Also more remittances from overseas contract workers are expected for the Christmas season, they said.
The meagre requirement of oil companies for the day, at $2.0 million, buoyed the peso, one trader said.
--LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
